title: Air Compressor Tank Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1926.306)
subtitle: Covers the 1926.306 air receiver rules; the standard itself sets no schedule for this check.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
Record each defect and the action taken, and recheck the item once it has been corrected.
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Construction and installation
items: For a receiver installed after the regulations' effective date, records or markings show it was built to ASME Section VIII, 1968 edition
Safety valves are constructed, installed and maintained to ASME Section VIII, 1968 edition
Every drain, handhole and manhole on the receiver is easily accessible
Receiver is not buried underground and is not in an inaccessible place

sections.title: Drains and traps
items: A drain pipe and valve are fitted at the lowest point of the receiver
Any automatic trap is in addition to the drain valve, which is still present and working
Receiver is drained completely and often enough that opening the drain valve releases no excessive oil or water

sections.title: Gages, safety valves and safety appliances
items: An indicating pressure gage is fitted and located so it is readily visible
At least one spring-loaded safety valve is fitted to the receiver
Combined relieving capacity of the safety valves holds pressure to no more than 10 percent above the receiver's MAWP
No valve before the safety valve
No valve of any type sits between the receiver and any of its safety valves
Safety valves, indicating devices and controlling devices cannot readily be made inoperative by any means, including weather
Safety valves are tested frequently and at regular intervals, and each valve is in good operating condition

references: 29 CFR 1926.306: Air receivers (Part 1926 Subpart I, Tools—Hand and Power)
